status: Proposed minimal child registration addendum; implementation qualification pending
scope: Four public helper signatures unchanged; only common.py, its contract tests, and source-bound evidence change. No scheduler, production lifecycle, generic supervisor, family worker, dependency or workflow changes.

protocol.endpoint: run_case opens one ephemeral loopback TCP registration listener before starting the worker. Its address and fresh per-run random authentication token are passed only in PLATO_PHASE4_REGISTRATION. Token is never included in result environment allowlists or logs. TCP avoids Unix socket pathname limits in owned pytest directories.
protocol.request: emit(child_started) records durable child_pid/child_created plus fresh registration_id and reporter pid/create_time, then synchronously requests registration. One newline-delimited JSON request bounded to 8192 bytes contains run token, case_id, registration_id, reporter pid/create_time and child pid/create_time. Other event types remain append-only.
protocol.identity: Server authenticates token and case, verifies the reporter is a live already-owned process with matching pid/create_time, then independently checks the child pid/create_time and current actual OS session or verified owned parent lineage. Reporter assertion alone is never authorization. It retains the independently proven child identity before responding and stores a registration receipt tied to case, request, reporter and child identities.
protocol.ack: Response binds registration_id, reporter identity and child identity and has registered or already_gone disposition. emit releases only after validating this response. Already_gone is allowed solely when the exact claimed identity is absent, zombie, or PID has a different create_time; it adds no owned identity and grants no signaling authority. A live matching unrelated child is rejected.
protocol.timing: Client has one total five-second connect/send/response deadline. Server bounds each accepted connection to one second and 8192 bytes, with serialized registrations and a 50ms accept timeout. Overall run_case timeout remains the authored <=180 seconds. No retry or silent success on failure.
protocol.worker_rule: Every controlled worker must call emit(child_started, child_pid=..., child_created=...) immediately after creating a child and before success, detachment/reparenting or terminating its owning process. Because emit is synchronous, a fast parent cannot pass its registration point and call os._exit before the supervisor records live OS ownership. Children may already use start_new_session=True at Popen; their actual parent lineage still exists while emit blocks.
protocol.local_failure_cleanup: Before requesting registration, emit independently observes whether the exact child is an actual descendant of the reporting process. On rejection, timeout, missing listener, or EOF, it emits a failure and raises. It may contain only this locally OS-proven exact child on that failure path (TERM <=1s then KILL <=1s with create-time checks); a valid/stale unrelated PID is never locally signaled. This handles supervisor termination before acknowledgment without authorizing cleanup from an assertion alone.
protocol.server_cleanup: run_case keeps OS polling and parser-independent owned cleanup. Registration acceptance retains actual OS proof, so accepted detached children remain owned after reparenting. Listener/registration thread is closed and joined boundedly in finally, without preventing existing process containment, pipe draining or durable result writing. Forced process cleanup still fails.
protocol.direct_event_writes: After containment, every durable child_started hint is independently classified. A live exact candidate lacking matching accepted registration or retained actual OS ownership produces a qualification error and is never signaled solely on that event. No positive success is possible from unresolved live child hints. Direct event writes bypassing emit are unsupported worker behavior; an unproven detached orphan cannot safely be killed from its claim. Regression owner recovers only exact children that its own controlled fixture actually spawned.
protocol.termination_before_ack: If the supervisor terminates, emit sees EOF/connection failure or expires its total deadline, cleans only its independently observed descendant, records local failure and raises; no success follows. If the reporter terminates mid-request, server rejects absent reporter or records independently proven ownership before any ack; known owned identities still receive bounded normal cleanup. Unknown live child hints fail without a signal. Abrupt bypass of emit cannot earn qualification.
protocol.trust_boundary: Authentication binds a request to this run and detects stale/cross-case/mismatched responses; OS parent/session proof supplies cleanup authorization. This is a controlled test-worker protocol, not a sandbox against malicious arbitrary worker code. A worker may not suppress registration exceptions and claim success; supervisor independently verifies durable hints and failure events anyway.

numeric_event_repair: Reject numeric identities that are non-int/float, non-finite, oversized or otherwise cannot be normalized without overflow. Catch OverflowError as a malformed event error. Event validation remains unable to bypass prior owned cleanup or durable stdout/stderr/result writing.
regressions: Exact review fast detached DEVNULL child with emit and immediate os._exit: must fail with retained owned child, forced containment and no survivor, repeated with no polling manipulation.
Direct file child_started bypass followed by immediate parent exit: unresolved live hint fails, is never automatically signaled; fixture finally recovers its exact controlled child.
Valid and stale unrelated PID/create_time markers: registration rejected or already_gone; unrelated process stays alive and outside owned identities.
Natural attached/detached genuine children and existing stalled-child cases retain behavior.

Rejected, wrong run token, never acknowledged, missing listener and reporter/supervisor termination registration paths are bounded failures; only independently proven local/parent owned children are signaled.
Oversized created and monotonic values produce malformed durable failure with stdout/stderr/result and no owned survivors; undecodable/unreadable/malformed probes remain green.
Focused typing/Ruff, current70 and existing245 policy contracts, preserved exact collections and all399 source hashes remain green; draft tasks remain ineligible.
review_boundary: Root and independent design reviewer must accept this exact small protocol addendum before implementing its dependent behavior. Numeric durability repair and reproduction evidence proceed independently.
